data.body_html:
The Sotogrande Polo Final 2044 is the season's most glamorous day on the Costa del Sol, and arriving by boat from Marbella turns the journey into part of the celebration. With Puerto Banús as your starting point, you can cruise 35 nautical miles south along the coast, anchor for a swim near Cala del Faro, and still reach the Santa María Polo Club in time for the trophy lift. Whether you're in a group of five or twelve, our fleet has the right vessel — and every charter includes a skipper, drinks, and snacks, so you can focus on the match.

Why take a boat to the Sotogrande Polo Final?

Driving from Marbella to Sotogrande takes about 45 minutes on a good day, but on final day the AP-7 and N-340 clog up with Range Rovers and vintage Land Cruisers. A boat avoids the traffic entirely, adds a Mediterranean backdrop, and lets you arrive at the marina steps rather than a dusty car park. You also get the freedom to anchor off the coast before the match, with the Sierra Bermeja behind you and the Guadiaro estuary ahead.

Distance and timing from Puerto Banús

The direct route from Puerto Banús to Sotogrande Marina is about 35 nautical miles. On a planing boat like the Pershing 46 or Mangusta 80, you'll cover this in 1.5–2 hours at 20–25 knots. We suggest departing at 13:00, grabbing a light lunch onboard, and arriving by 15:00 to settle in before the final starts. If you want to make a day of it, leave at 11:00 and stop at Cala del Faro for a swim.

Best boats for your group

Our fleet covers groups from 5 to 12 passengers. For a couple or small family, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are ideal — both start at €749 for 2 hours, with skipper, drinks, and snacks included. For a larger entourage, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) is the showstopper: from €4,719 for a minimum of 4 hours, and a jet ski is thrown in free. Other superyachts like the Ferretti 94 or Canados 86 are available on request via WhatsApp.

What's included in every charter

  • Licensed skipper (speaks English and Spanish)
  • Fuel for the entire trip
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava
  • Light snacks (olives, crisps, nuts)
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%) — no surprises

On Tier B boats like the Mangusta 80, a jet ski is also included at no extra cost — perfect for a pre-match adrenaline hit.

Anchoring and arriving at the polo club

The Santa María Polo Club sits on the Guadiaro estuary, but the river mouth is shallow and subject to strong currents. Most of our skippers anchor at Cala del Faro or just off the marina breakwater, then use a tender to get you ashore. From there it's a 10-minute walk or a short taxi ride to the club entrance. If you prefer to dock, Sotogrande Marina has visitor berths — let us know when booking and we'll arrange it.

What to expect on the day

August in Marbella means 30°C heat and a light sea breeze. Your skipper will keep the cooler stocked with chilled cava and beer, and you can swim off the back platform before the match. After the final, the atmosphere in Sotogrande is electric — many guests choose to stay for dinner at one of the marina's restaurants. If you want to return to Marbella the same day, we'll have you back in Puerto Banús by 21:00.

Book your boat for the final

August is peak season, and the polo final is one of the busiest days on the coast. We recommend booking at least 3–4 months in advance to secure your preferred vessel. To reserve, simply browse our fleet and send us a WhatsApp message — we'll confirm availability and send a booking link. No payment is taken until you confirm, and cancellations up to 14 days before are fully refunded.
